name: spo-report-sensitivity-label-coverage
title: Report sensitivity label coverage for Copilot readiness
shortDescription: Reports how many documents in a site are unlabeled - the content Microsoft 365 Copilot would surface with no sensitivity classification - and ranks the gaps worst-covered library first.
longDescription: Before turning Microsoft 365 Copilot loose on a site, you want to know how much of the content has a sensitivity label and how much does not, because an unlabeled document is one Copilot can surface and summarise with no classification attached. This read-only script answers that. It uses SharePoint Search (the crawled managed property InformationProtectionLabelId, which holds the label GUID and is empty when a document is unlabeled) to count labeled versus unlabeled documents without walking every file, so it scales across large libraries. It groups the result per library, ranks the worst-covered first, prints a site coverage percentage and a plain Copilot-exposure line, and can also write a CSV of every document and a styled HTML report. It complements Microsoft Purview rather than replacing it: Purview owns applying labels (auto-labeling, default labels); this just finds where labels are missing so you can target them, and it is useful even on tenants without the premium auto-labeling licences. It reflects the search index, so freshly uploaded, migrated, or just-labeled documents will not show correct status until they have been crawled.
